name: Ban62
role: Tech Lead · Frontend · Business Analysis · 2-person team
summary: A multi-concept ordering, queue-management, and payment system built for daily use in a family-run food business.

detail.introduction: A web-based ordering, queue-management, and payment system built to replace physical queue tickets for a family-run food business operating multiple restaurant concepts under one roof. Customers can pre-order remotely via QR code, track their place in line in real time, and staff can manage orders, menus, and revenue across every concept from one dashboard. The system is built and deployed for actual daily use, not as a demo.
detail.problem: The paper-ticket queue system had recurring failures: tickets were lost and had to be reprinted, customers could not cancel orders, and there was no way to pre-order before arriving. Without payment commitment, no-shows and fake orders were common. One shared system also needed to serve several restaurant concepts, each with its own menu, staff, and reporting, without data or workflows bleeding between them.
detail.architecture: Frontend: Nuxt with TypeScript, Tailwind, and Pinia, deployed on Vercel. Backend: .NET modular monolith organized into Api/Application/Domain/Infrastructure Clean Architecture layers, with a custom Mediator pattern and pipeline behaviors, deployed on Render. Data: PostgreSQL via EF Core on Neon. Real time: SignalR pushes queue and order-status updates to customer and staff views. Payments: price-locked PromptPay QR codes are generated by the system, and bank slips are verified server-side before orders enter the kitchen queue.
detail.challenge: Verify payments server-side before orders reach the kitchen without requiring customer accounts; identify repeat customers using a cookie-based Client ID to support order history and enforce cancellation windows; and isolate data and permissions for multiple restaurant concepts on one shared codebase and database.
highlights: Built and deployed for a real family-run restaurant business
Led frontend and DevOps work in a 2-person team
Verified PromptPay payments before orders enter the kitchen queue
Supported multiple restaurant concepts through one isolated system

name: Suvlet Portfolio
summary: A personal portfolio and lightweight CMS for the Suvlet lofi/jazzhop music project, designed to feel minimal, fast, and smooth while keeping all content manageable without touching code.

detail.overview: A personal portfolio and lightweight CMS platform built for my music project "Suvlet" (lofi/jazzhop). The site is designed to be minimal, fast, and smooth to scroll through, guiding visitors along a simple path: discover the artist, listen to highlighted work, browse the full discography, and get in touch. Beyond the public-facing site, the project includes a full admin dashboard so all content can be managed without ever touching code.
detail.problem: Build a music-focused portfolio experience and a CMS flexible enough to manage public content without redeploying or editing code.
detail.architecture: Frontend: Nuxt with Pinia for state management, Tailwind for styling, and WaveSurfer.js for binary audio waveform rendering on the Genre page. Backend: .NET with FastEndpoints following Vertical Slice Architecture, with FluentValidation for request validation and JWT-based admin authentication. Data layer: PostgreSQL via EF Core hosted on Neon. File storage: Cloudflare R2, integrated through the AWS S3 SDK for cover art and audio files. Deployment: Cloudflare Pages for the frontend and Render for the backend API.
detail.challenge: The core challenge was not the public site itself, but building a CMS flexible enough to let a non-developer manage nested, structured content such as releases with variable-length tracklists, a discography grouped dynamically by year, and unreleased feature toggles, all without hardcoding content or redeploying for each update.
highlights: Handled both Fullstack and DevOps responsibilities
Built a zero-code admin workflow for music content management
Integrated WaveSurfer.js for a richer listening experience
Separated frontend, API, storage, and database across Cloudflare Pages, Render, R2, and Neon

name: BNI Miracle
summary: A business-networking platform with an admin management portal and a visitor site for member content, events, deals, and reports.

detail.introduction: BNI Miracle is a web platform built to support data and activity management for a business networking group, covering both an admin-side management portal and a visitor-facing site. Internship work focused on developing and improving UI screens and components on both sides to meet the defined requirements.
detail.problem: Admins needed one interface to manage varied content such as member groups, showcases, reports, One Page content, and Hot Deals without maintaining a separate hardcoded form for each. Visitors needed clean, mobile-friendly pages for Hot Deals, events, and showcases, a way to report issues, and support for visitors who are not authenticated through LINE login.
detail.architecture: Admin UI: built or improved group and member management, showcase creation, report management and detail views, One Page and Hot Deal management, mobile previews for One Page/Event/Hot Deal, and a Dynamic Form–based contact form. Visitor UI: improved Hot Deal, Event, Showcase, and Report a Problem pages, and redesigned the One Page Flex Card section for a more consistent experience. Feature work: added admin-editable Dynamic Forms, anonymous visitor tracking for usage data, and Report a Problem flows. Testing: verified API input/output with Swagger and Postman, tested user flows against real scenarios, and documented results before handoff. The project stack includes Vue/Nuxt, TypeScript, Pinia, Tailwind CSS, Axios, .NET, FastEndpoints, EF Core, PostgreSQL, Docker, and LINE/LIFF.
detail.challenge: Design a Dynamic Form system flexible enough to support varied admin-editable data structures without hardcoding a form per content type; implement anonymous visitor tracking without LINE login; and make the One Page Flex Card experience visually consistent across Hot Deal, Event, and Showcase content.
highlights: Contributed across admin and visitor-facing interfaces
Built a Dynamic Form feature for admin-editable content
Added anonymous visitor tracking and Report a Problem flows
Tested API and UI behavior and documented results before handoff

name: FandomEngine
summary: An artist portfolio and creative-content platform, with a reusable frontend foundation built during Phase 1 of an internship.

detail.introduction: FandomEngine is a web platform for presenting artists' portfolios and creative content. During Phase 1 of the internship, I worked largely independently from initial project setup and mockups through building the core UI, guided by the internship mentor and the study's defined requirements.
detail.problem: The platform needed a scalable frontend foundation from day one: consistent folder and component structure, clear routing, and reusable components, so later pages and features such as multiple artist display formats, campaigns, and events could be added without reworking earlier work.
detail.architecture: Project setup: established folder structure, file and module naming conventions, and baseline routing and component separation. Mockups: built UI mockups to align with the mentor on user flows and key interactions before implementation. Core UI: developed Register, Home, Artist, Campaign, Event, and Profile pages, with Group and Solo artist formats built from reusable components. Staging: deployed the project for pre-production testing of core flows before requesting review. Bug fixing: investigated issues using logs, observed behavior, requirements, and mentor feedback, then applied targeted fixes and re-tested.
detail.challenge: Designing a component and routing structure upfront that could support Group and Solo artist views, Campaign, Event, and Profile pages without structural rework, while balancing mockup-driven UI validation with delivering working pages within Phase 1's timeline.
highlights: Worked largely independently under internship mentor direction
Established the initial project structure and mockups
Built Register, Home, Artist, Campaign, Event, and Profile pages
Supported Group and Solo artist layouts with reusable components
Deployed to staging and verified fixes against requirements

name: SSO Chatbot
role: AI Engineer · Testing · Group thesis project
summary: A source-grounded RAG chatbot that helps staff and insured persons look up Thai social security benefits and rights.

detail.introduction: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation chatbot built as a university thesis project to help Social Security Office staff and insured persons look up information about insured persons' benefits and rights. It is modeled after a Thai government labor agency and is not affiliated with the real agency. A locally-run LLM served through Ollama answers questions using a Pinecone index built from benefit documentation, through a Chainlit chat interface.
detail.problem: Staff at Social Security branch offices, especially smaller regional branches with less specialized knowledge, had to manually cross-reference documents to answer questions about cash compensation, medical treatment rights, and other benefits. This made responses slow and inconsistent, depending heavily on individual experience. There was no centralized way for staff or insured persons to get fast, source-grounded answers to natural-language questions and conversational follow-ups.
detail.architecture: Ingestion: documents are pulled from Google Drive API, cleaned, sanitized, sentence-split, and embedded with HuggingFace multilingual-e5-large-instruct through LlamaIndex. Retrieval: Pinecone stores vectors with namespaces and metadata for filtered retrieval, with similarity thresholding to control result quality. Generation: an Ollama-hosted local LLM creates answers grounded in retrieved chunks using engineered prompts. Query understanding: intent classification and off-topic detection filter out-of-scope questions, while query rewriting uses conversation context for follow-ups. Interface: Chainlit. Reliability and local configuration: Tenacity retries with exponential backoff, SQLite3, and python-dotenv.
detail.challenge: Keep answers grounded in source documents and minimize hallucinations where incorrect benefit information could have real consequences; reliably detect and decline out-of-scope questions rather than letting the LLM guess; tune sentence splitting and similarity thresholds for Thai legal and benefits documents using a multilingual embedding model; and rewrite conversational follow-ups with prior context before retrieval.
highlights: Built as a university group thesis project
Used local LLM inference through Ollama
Grounded answers in retrieved benefit documentation
Added intent classification, off-topic filtering, and contextual query rewriting
